description: We are Meissa, a team passionate about technology and innovation. We aim to turn NASA Earth data into an engaging interactive experience. We welcome creative members interested in coding, design, and data visualization.
summary:
MarsMind is an interactive web platform designed to make exploring and understanding the Martian surface easier. Our project brings together terrain visualization, hazard assessment, and an interactive exploration assistant to help users examine different areas of Mars and understand the challenges of navigating its surface.

Exploring Mars involves more than choosing a destination. Differences in elevation, steep slopes, and potentially dangerous terrain can make movement difficult. MarsMind addresses this challenge by presenting terrain information in a clear, accessible way.

Users can explore an interactive Martian map, select locations, analyze elevation and slope, assess terrain hazards, and compare possible exploration routes based on distance and risk. The platform also includes an exploration assistant that helps users understand terrain conditions and Mars-related questions.

Our goal is to make planetary exploration more approachable while demonstrating how geographic information and software can support future mission planning, scientific education, and safer surface exploration.
details:
The Problem

Exploring Mars is challenging because its surface contains steep slopes, uneven terrain, and significant elevation changes. These conditions can make navigation difficult for rovers and future human missions.

Understanding terrain conditions is essential when choosing exploration routes. However, interpreting geographic data and evaluating potential risks can be complicated.

We wanted to make this process easier to understand through an interactive platform that brings Mars exploration and terrain analysis together.

Our Solution

We developed MarsMind, an interactive web application that helps users explore the Martian surface, analyze terrain conditions, and plan possible exploration routes.

MarsMind combines NASA Mars imagery, elevation data, terrain risk assessment, route planning, and an interactive exploration assistant in one platform.

Our goal is to help users understand the challenges of navigating Mars and explore how technology can support planetary exploration.

How MarsMind Works

1. Interactive Mars Map

Users can explore the Martian surface through an interactive map using NASA Mars Trek imagery. The platform allows users to examine selected locations and understand their geographic characteristics.

2. Terrain Analysis

MarsMind processes digital elevation data to calculate terrain characteristics such as elevation and slope.

Our project includes a regional elevation dataset for Jezero Crater derived from NASA's Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) mission data.

We also developed a separate synthetic dataset for demonstration and testing. These simulated values are clearly distinguished from actual Mars observations.

3. Terrain Risk Assessment

MarsMind uses a rule-based scoring system to evaluate terrain conditions.

Based primarily on slope measurements, the system classifies areas into different risk levels and identifies potentially traversable locations.

This helps users understand how terrain characteristics may influence rover navigation. The results are educational estimates rather than validated mission-safety assessments.

4. Route Planning

Users can choose starting and destination points to explore possible paths across the terrain.

The application calculates and compares a shortest route with a lower-risk alternative, taking terrain characteristics into account.

It also estimates route distance, travel time, and energy requirements using simplified rover movement assumptions.

This feature helps demonstrate the trade-offs between travel efficiency and terrain risk.

5. ARES Exploration Assistant

MarsMind includes ARES, an interactive assistant designed to help users understand Mars exploration concepts.

The assistant provides information about the Martian environment, atmospheric conditions, life-support systems, communication delays, and exploration challenges.

It also includes simulated mission scenarios, allowing users to explore situations such as dust storms and other operational challenges.

The system supports predefined responses and optional AI-powered functionality, depending on configuration.

Technologies Used

Our team developed MarsMind using a combination of modern web technologies and geographic data processing tools.

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and Vite.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Data Processing: NumPy and digital elevation model (DEM) analysis.
  • NASA Resources: NASA Mars Trek imagery and Mars Global Surveyor MOLA elevation data.
  • Route Planning: Custom JavaScript pathfinding and terrain-based route calculations.
  • Assistant: Python-based conversational functionality with optional language-model integration.
  • Development Tools: Git and GitHub for version control and collaboration.

What Makes MarsMind Different?

We wanted to create more than a visualization of Mars.

MarsMind allows users to interact with terrain information, understand potential navigation difficulties, and compare different exploration routes.

One of our main design decisions was to make the terrain analysis explainable. Instead of relying on a complex prediction model, we used measurable characteristics such as slope to generate understandable risk classifications.

We also combined the scientific aspects of Mars exploration with an accessible interface and a conversational assistant to create a more engaging learning experience.

Challenges and Design Decisions

One of our challenges was processing elevation data and turning it into meaningful information for users.

We needed to calculate terrain slopes, identify potentially difficult areas, and make those results understandable through the interface.

Another challenge was developing route calculations that consider both distance and terrain risk.

We chose a rule-based approach because it is transparent, relatively lightweight, and suitable for an educational prototype.

We also considered data accuracy. Our project distinguishes actual NASA-derived elevation data from synthetic demonstration data, and we recognize that the resolution of MOLA data is not sufficient to identify individual rocks or small rover-scale obstacles.

Intended Impact

MarsMind demonstrates how NASA data and accessible software tools can help people better understand planetary exploration.

The project can support STEM education, interactive scientific demonstrations, and early-stage exploration concepts.

We hope to continue developing MarsMind by improving terrain visualization, expanding geographic coverage, and introducing more advanced navigation capabilities.

Our vision is to make exploring Mars more understandable, interactive, and accessible to students, researchers, and anyone interested in space exploration.
